sections.h2: Exchange prices rose about 50% in a month as scarcity hit the market

chart.title: Day-ahead prices rose from ₹4.88 to ₹7.3 per unit between August and September
chart.sub: Average day-ahead market clearing price, ₹ per kWh.
chart.source: IEX via Mercom and JM Financial.

sections.means: Buy bids on the exchange rose 281% year-on-year on 10 September while day-ahead volume rose only 0.5%, so far more was bid than cleared.
sections.todo: Check IEX's October figures, due in early November, to see whether the 25 September order has cooled prices.

sections.h2: Coal stock at power plants stayed above 18 MT, so the squeeze is not a fuel shortage

chart.title: Plant stock fell 0.24 MT a day in September but only 0.06 MT a day in early October
chart.sub: Average daily change in coal stock at domestic power plants, million tonnes per day.
chart.source: Ministry of Coal via All India Radio.

sections.means: Plants held roughly seven days of coal at the current burn, so the post reads the stock as fuel in the yard rather than a shortage of power.
sections.todo: Track the weekly CEA captive reports, which are not public, to measure how much surplus the 112 plants actually offer.

sections.h2: Coal rakes loaded for the power sector rose to 469 a day in early October

chart.title: Rakes loaded for the power sector rose from 426 to 469 a day
chart.sub: Rakes loaded per day for the power sector.
chart.source: Ministry of Coal via Indian Masterminds.

sections.means: Coal supplied to the power sector rose from 2.21 MT a day in September to 2.49 MT a day in 1–10 October.
sections.todo: Check whether that supply rise holds once captive plants start burning more under the 1 October order.
